value: A classic white grown in Geneva beside the traditional Chasselas, among the international grapes the canton has added to its vineyard.
source_notes: swissinfo: Chasselas and Gamay gradually replaced with Chardonnay and Pinot Noir; Decanter (Geneva guide): international varieties like Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay now commonly grown in Geneva; Swiss Wine Promotion Geneva page: Chasselas remains dominant white, Geneva winemakers have had success with Chardonnay.

value: The main white grape of Geneva, traditionally grown beside Gamay as one of the canton's two everyday wines.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion: Chasselas remains the dominant white grape variety in Geneva; Decanter: most produced grapes in Geneva are Chasselas for white and Gamay for red, historically the easy drinking wines; swissinfo: Chasselas and Gamay traditionally the main grapes grown in Geneva.

value: In Geneva, Chasselas is fresh and light, with delicate fruit and a mineral touch, made above all for drinking as an aperitif.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion Geneva page: Chasselas characterised by freshness, minerality and delicate fruitiness; Geneve Terroir (cantonal promotion office): a fresh, light wine that makes an ideal aperitif.

value: A Swiss cross of Gamay and Reichensteiner grown in Geneva both on its own and blended with its sibling Garanoir, as in the Esprit de Genève red blends.
source_notes: Geneve Terroir: Gamaret and Garanoir, both crosses of Gamay and Reichensteiner, among newest varieties planted in Geneva; The Wine Society (Ellen Wallace): Esprit de Geneve blend by top Geneva growers uses cousin grapes gamaret and garanoir; Decanter: Gamaret and Garanoir crosses of Gamay and Reichensteiner, sommelier recommends a Geneva Gamaret; swissinfo: Gamaret Garanoir blend at a Geneva winery.

value: Geneva's main red grape and the source of its best known red wine, traditionally grown beside Chasselas.
source_notes: Geneve Terroir: Geneva's best known red wine is made from Gamay; Decanter: most produced grapes are Chasselas for white and Gamay for red; Swiss Wine Promotion: among red wines Gamay holds first place; swissinfo: Chasselas and Gamay traditionally the main grapes.

value: In Geneva, Gamay is usually fruity and soft in tannin, though the best wines are more structured, with red fruit and spice.
source_notes: Geneve Terroir: often fruity and low in tannins, Gamay can also be structured with aromas of red fruit and spices; Swiss Wine Promotion Geneva page: Gamay gives excellent wines, very well structured; Decanter: Gamay historically one of Geneva's easy drinking wines.

value: Long grown in Geneva, where it is one of the main red grapes beside Gamay.
source_notes: Geneve Terroir: Pinot Noir has long been grown in Geneva; Swiss Wine Promotion Geneva page: red wines from Gamay, Pinot Noir in each of the canton's areas, Pinot Noir gaining ground; Decanter: Pinot Noir now commonly grown in Geneva.

value: In Geneva, Pinot Noir is fine and elegant, with raspberry and blackberry fruit and smooth tannins, and it takes well to oak ageing.
source_notes: Geneve Terroir: distinguished, fine and classy wines with fruity notes of raspberry and blackberry that lend themselves well to oak ageing; Swiss Wine Promotion Geneva page (rive gauche): Gamay and Pinot Noir reds characterised by elegance and smooth tannins.

value: Riesling x Silvaner
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion Graubuenden page lists the white as Riesling x Silvaner; Canton of Graubuenden vineyard statistics (Plantahof) name the variety Riesling-Silvaner (hyphen removed here per house style; Swiss Wine spelling kept); Swiss Wine Promotion grape page: the name Riesling-Silvaner was retained in Switzerland.

value: Grauburgunder
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion grape page: Pinot Gris is called Grauburgunder in German speaking Switzerland; Graubuenden cantonal wine regulation 917.400 Art. 24 uses Grauburgunder (Grau- oder Weissburgunder); cantonal vineyard statistics list Grauburgunder. None shows a Graubuenden label directly.

value: Graubünden's main grape, dominant in the Bündner Herrschaft and the Chur Rhine valley, made mostly as red but also as rosé, including Œil de Perdrix.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion Graubuenden page: Pinot Noir (Blauburgunder) is the primary grape, dominant in the Buendner Herrschaft; Graubuenden Viva factsheet (cantonal programme): Blauburgunder dominates the Buendner Herrschaft and Churer Rheintal, styles from light and powerful reds to rosé, blanc de noir and sparkling; cantonal regulation 917.400 Art. 24: Oeil de Perdrix is an AOC rosé from Blauburgunder.

value: In Graubünden, Blauburgunder is elegant, with fine berry fruit and a mineral backbone from the chalky soils, ripened by the warm foehn wind.
source_notes: Graubuenden Viva factsheet: elegant wines with fine berry aromas, shaped by the foehn and mineral soils, calcareous slate soils; Decanter (Burgundy with Altitude): foehn intensifies fruit character while leaving the wines with a distinctly mineral backbone, warm summers and cool nights preserve tension and freshness.

value: The main grape of Lavaux, grown on terraced slopes above Lake Geneva, and the grape behind the Dézaley and Calamin Grand Cru whites.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion Vaud page: Lavaux is the birthplace of great white wines, particularly Chasselas, the region's emblematic grape; Decanter (Discover the grapes of Vaud): Dezaley and Calamin, Vaud's only grand cru vineyards, give a yin and yang experience of Chasselas; Canton of Vaud vineyard register: Chasselas by far the largest variety in Lavaux.

value: In Lavaux, Chasselas tends to be fuller and more mineral than elsewhere in Vaud, from the sunny, terraced slopes above the lake.
source_notes: Decanter: Lavaux slopes with poorer soils and sun reflected from the lake; its wines tend to be fuller, more mineral and ageworthy; Swiss Wine Promotion Vaud page: Lavaux produces wines of remarkable finesse and minerality, with the three suns of sky, lake and stone walls.

value: In Neuchâtel, Chasselas is lively and fresh, with a fine mineral edge from the limestone soils.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion Three Lakes page: best known whites here are lively Chasselas; limestone soils favour elegant, fresh wines particularly from Chasselas; Hachette guide (AOC Neuchatel reviews of individual Chasselas): belle vivacite, fine trame minerale, vivacite en phase avec sa mineralite. Hachette source is producer wine reviews, not a regional description.

value: Neuchâtel's main red grape, made as red wine and as Œil de Perdrix, the pale rosé that is a speciality of the canton.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion Three Lakes page: Pinot Noir is the most widely grown red in Neuchatel, producing reds and the Oeil de Perdrix rosé that originated in Neuchatel; Hachette: oeil de perdrix, the speciality that made the Neuchatel vineyard famous, from pinot noir; The Wine Society: oeil de perdrix, a rosé from pinot noir, in Neuchatel Vully.

value: One of the white grapes recommended in Ticino, a minor variety in a canton planted mainly with red Merlot.
source_notes: Ticino Turismo: for white grapes Chardonnay, Chasselas, Semillon, Sauvignon Blanc ... are recommended; Merlot covers about 80 percent; Ticinowine (interprofession): Chardonnay listed among white grapes, which are a small share of the vineyard, Merlot the leading grape.

value: In Ticino, Merlot is soft and smooth from the warmer clay soils of the south, and fresher and leaner from the stony soils north of Monte Ceneri.
source_notes: Ticinowine: south of Monte Ceneri clay rich soils and warmer climate give wines of great elegance and softness; north, stony moraine soils and alpine climate give austere wines for long ageing; Swiss Wine Promotion Ticino page: Sopraceneri granite soils give minerality and freshness, Merlot lighter and more elegant; Sottoceneri warmer, powerful full bodied Merlot, smoother and more intense.

value: One of the white grapes recommended in Ticino, a minor variety in a canton planted mainly with red Merlot.
source_notes: Ticino Turismo: Sauvignon Blanc among recommended white grapes; Merlot about 80 percent; Ticinowine: Sauvignon Bianco listed among white grapes, a small share of the vineyard.

value: Fendant is the traditional Valais name for AOC wine made only from Chasselas, with no other grape allowed, and the name is reserved for Valais.
source_notes: Valais Ordonnance sur la vigne et le vin Art. 49: Le Fendant est un vin AOC du Valais issu exclusivement du cepage Chasselas; toute adjonction est interdite (version fetched shows amendments to 2016); Swiss Wine Promotion: the Fendant appellation has been protected in Valais and refers exclusively to Chasselas wines produced in the canton.

value: In Valais, Fendant is light and easy, with a mineral, sometimes flinty touch drawn from the soils.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Valais (interprofession): fruity with a mineral character (flint, hazelnut) due to the terroir; light and easy to drink; Swiss Wine Promotion: the mineral note derived from the terroir of regions such as Valais is particularly characteristic.

value: A native red that in Switzerland grows only in Valais; it ripens late and is difficult in the vineyard, and is bottled as a single variety wine.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion: emblematic red of Valais where it is exclusively grown, difficult to cultivate; Swiss Wine Valais: matures late, a capricious grape, nearly abandoned; The Wine Society: cornalin, a difficult grape; Valais ordinance Art. 56: Cornalin or Rouge du Pays is an AOC Valais wine from Cornalin du Valais.

value: In Valais, Cornalin is deeply coloured, juicy and fresh, with silky tannins.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion: colourful, fruity and juicy wines with silky tannins; Swiss Wine Valais: deep cherry red colour, body energetic and very fresh, smooth fruit, elegant mouthfeel.

value: The partner of Pinot Noir in Dôle, where Pinot Noir must lead, and also bottled on its own.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Valais: blended with Pinot Noir it becomes Dôle; vinified alone also described; Swiss Wine Promotion: in Switzerland Gamay often vinified alone, also in Dôle with Pinot Noir; Valais ordinance Art. 55: Dôle from Pinot noir alone or at least 85 percent Pinot noir and Gamay, Pinot noir dominating.

value: Brought from the Aosta Valley over the Great St Bernard Pass, it grows in Switzerland almost only in Valais, where it ranks as the second native red after Cornalin.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion: introduced in Valais from the Aosta Valley, grown almost exclusively in Valais; Swiss Wine Valais: introduced via the Great Saint Bernard pass, after Cornalin the second great red wine with a Valais identity.

value: In Valais, Humagne Rouge is rustic in character, with wild berry fruit and earthy, woody notes.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Valais: rustic aromas of wild fruits, wooded undergrowth, bark, violets; oak bark characteristic; Swiss Wine Promotion: aromas of violet, dried vine leaf, elderberry, smoke; The Wine Society: humagne rouge, a rustic red.

value: A native white grown almost only in Valais; it ripens late and needs the sunniest sites, and is made dry and as sweet wine from overripe grapes.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Valais: ripens late, demands the most exposure to sun; nervy dry version, slightly sweet version and sweet withered grape wines; Swiss Wine Promotion: grown almost exclusively in Valais, sunny steep slopes, most wines dry but also noble sweet; Valais ordinance Art. 90 (Grand Cru chapter): vin surmature, a sweet wine, may be made from Arvine.

value: In Valais, Petite Arvine is intense and lively, with marked acidity in both its dry and sweet wines.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Valais: complex, concentrated and intense, acidity can be high; Swiss Wine Promotion: intense aromas, fresh with lively but well integrated acidity.

value: Brought from the northern Rhône, Syrah thrives in the dry, sunny and windy climate of Valais, where most Swiss Syrah grows.
source_notes: Swiss Wine Promotion: introduced to Valais from the Rhone, adapted to the dry, hot and windy climate, majority of vines in Valais; Swiss Wine Valais: brought to the canton from the Rhone, found a second home; Decanter (Six Swiss Syrah): Valais sunny, windy and dry, home to most Swiss Syrah.

value: In Valais, Syrah is perfumed and elegant, with a peppery, spicy lift that recalls the cooler northern Rhône.
source_notes: Decanter (Six Swiss Syrah): Valais is a cool climate extension of the northern Rhone and its Syrahs taste perfumed, spicy, weightless, graceful; peppercorns an aromatic marker; Swiss Wine Valais: spices, black pepper, wild berries, classy tannins, powerful and elegant, compared with northern Rhone Syrah.

value: A minor white in Vaud, grown on a small scale beside the dominant Chasselas.
source_notes: Decanter (grapes of Vaud): Chasselas so dominant that Chardonnay totals only a small share of plantings; Canton of Vaud press release: Chasselas largely dominant, Chardonnay and Pinot gris together cover a small share of white vineyards.

value: The main grape and signature white of Vaud, whose style changes from La Côte to Lavaux and Chablais.
source_notes: Decanter: Chasselas is the region's grande dame, reveals various expressions in La Cote, Lavaux and Chablais; Swiss Wine Promotion Vaud page: canton Vaud reveres its emblematic grape, Chasselas, reflecting the diversity of soils; Canton of Vaud: Chasselas remains the largely dominant grape.

value: In Vaud, Chasselas runs from soft and delicate on La Côte to broader, stonier and more powerful wines in Chablais.
source_notes: Decanter: La Cote produces softer structured, more delicate wines; Chablais wines broad, concentrated and moderately powerful with stony undertones; Swiss Wine Promotion Vaud page: La Cote Chasselas fresh, fruity and floral; Chablais Chasselas displays powerful, slightly salty notes and pronounced minerality.

value: Bred at the Agroscope research station at Pully in Vaud from Gamay and Reichensteiner, it is grown in Vaud mostly for red blends and also made as a single variety wine.
source_notes: Decanter: Gamaret and Garanoir, crosses of Gamay and Reichensteiner created by Agroscope; many reds blended, Gamaret a particular success as a varietal wine; Swiss Wine Promotion: created at Agroscope in Pully, often used as a blend component; Canton of Vaud press release: gamaret and garanoir boost Vaud reds.

value: One of Vaud's main red grapes beside Pinot Noir, made alone or in blends, and also grown as Plant Robert, an old local form of Gamay.
source_notes: Decanter: most planted reds Pinot Noir, Gamay including Plant Robert, a rare ancient Gamay biotype, Gamaret and Garanoir; many reds blended; Swiss Wine Promotion Vaud page: red wines made from Gamay and Pinot Noir; The Wine Society: plant robert, a red brought back from the brink of extinction around Morges and Lausanne.

value: One of Vaud's main red grapes beside Gamay, also kept near Morges as Servagnin, an old local strain.
source_notes: Decanter: Pinot Noir among the most planted reds in Vaud; Swiss Wine Promotion Vaud page: reds made from Gamay and Pinot Noir; The Wine Society: servagnin, a strain of pinot noir, around Morges; Swiss Wine Promotion grape page: in Vaud Pinot Noir grown since the 15th century, originally under the name Servagnin.
